title: botai contribution
description: One piece of work a student is preparing to offer to a course repository. The record exists to keep three claims apart that are easy to blur: what the student says they did, what a local command observed, and what the remote actually accepted. Only the last is ACCEPTED, and it never comes from a model's text.

session_id.description: The teaching session this contribution came out of, or null when the student starts contributing outside a session. null is honest here: inventing a session id would attach the work to a sitting that never happened.

role.description: Expert, researcher or developer. A documentation fix and a code change are both contributions; this records which kind of work is being prepared.

task_ref.description: Link or local description of the task, as the student gave it.

base_oid.description: The commit the work started from. A real Git OID or null — a course without its own repository has no OID to report.

diff_hash.description: Digest of the change as observed. A force-push or a reopened PR changes it, which invalidates the checks recorded against the older revision rather than silently carrying them over.

checks.description: An empty list does not satisfy LOCAL_CHECKED: either every required check passed, or the role's non-programmatic checks are recorded explicitly.

confirmed_by_learner.description: Set only from a human channel. A value arriving from a model proposal stays model_reported and does not authorise publication.

external_ref.description: The PR URL or id, once one exists.

observation_source.description: How the last transition was learned. `learner_report` is kept distinct from `remote_api`: a student saying they opened a PR is information, not verification.
